title: Renin-Angiotensin System Inhibition in Advanced Chronic Kidney Disease
authors: Bhandari S, Mehta S, Khwaja A, Cleland JGF, Ives N, Brettell E, et al.; STOP ACEi Trial Investigators
population: Patients in the United Kingdom with advanced and progressive chronic kidney disease (eGFR below 30 ml/min/1.73 m2) taking an ACE inhibitor or angiotensin receptor blocker
funder: Funded by the National Institute for Health Research and the Medical Research Council (statement in the published abstract). A post hoc analysis of the same trial gives the grant as NIHR-HTA 11/30/07 from the National Institute for Health Research and the Medical Research Council. The role of the funders is not stated in a readable source.
result: Open-label trial of discontinuing against continuing renin-angiotensin system inhibitors. At 3 years the least-squares mean eGFR was 12.6 against 13.3 ml/min/1.73 m2 (difference -0.7, 95% CI -2.5 to 1.0), with no heterogeneity across prespecified subgroups. End-stage kidney disease or kidney replacement therapy occurred in 128 (62%) after discontinuation and 115 (56%) with continuation (hazard ratio 1.28, 0.99 to 1.65). Cardiovascular events 108 against 88 and deaths 20 against 22.
